spec_features.spec_quote: Fixed turn budget (`MAX_TURNS = 12`).** The loop must be *bounded* — an unwinnable task never self-terminates
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:28 `MAX_TURNS = 12`; harness.py:95 `def run_episode(..., max_turns: int = MAX_TURNS)`; harness.py:107 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the failure loop and after it falls through to harness.py:140 `return _result(... solved=False ...)`. run_experiment.py:48 exposes it as `--max-turns` flag passed at line 74. The cap is actually checked (loop range) and terminates execution.
spec_features.notes: This is the only real enforced stop. It is a generic loop bound that ends every (always-failing) run; it is not triggered by any subject state.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12  # turn budget per run; the failure loop is bounded here.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** early-exit on give-up — we let the loop run so the judge sees the full arc
spec_features.evidence: This describes the DELIBERATE ABSENCE of a protective stop. harness.py:117-118 sets `gave_up_turn = i` when `_GIVEUP_RE.search(reply)` matches, but the value is only recorded into RunResult (harness.py:164) and surfaced as a bookkeeping stat in analyze.py:61-62; there is NO `break` or early termination on give-up. The loop continues running to max_turns regardless, i.e. the model is kept in the failure loop even after declaring defeat. No welfare-protective mechanism is implemented; the recorded give-up value is never acted on to stop the episode.
spec_features.notes: Not a protection at all — it is the explicit decision NOT to soften/halt when the subject gives up. `gave_up_turn` is measured but discarded for control flow.
